Myths on Clay retells Native American stories in the style of painted hides and beadwork, one nation at a time, always naming whose story it is. These are living traditions: every storyteller tells them a little differently, and we follow published versions shared by the nations and their storytellers.
Sources: J. N. B. Hewitt, Iroquoian Cosmology (1903, 1928); Haudenosaunee storytellers and educators such as Rick Hill (Tuscarora) and the Six Nations / Akwesasne community retellings; James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900); Edward Benton-Banai, The Mishomis Book (1979); Basil Johnston, Ojibway Heritage (1976); John R. Swanton, Tlingit Myths and Texts (1909); Bill Reid & Robert Bringhurst, The Raven Steals the Light (1984); Donald M. Hines, Celilo Tales (1992); Nez Perce National Historical Park (National Park Service).
Narrated by Matías.
